title: The five theorems of src/Main.lean
summary: RH (Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis) and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, in four forms. All five come from one theorem, New.grh: no Dirichlet L-function vanishes in re s > 1/2. RH and the critical-line forms then follow by the functional equation's symmetry s -> 1 - s (New/Main.lean). The boundaries below follow the authors' own reading guide (GUIDE.md, section 1, the topic table) and the volumes of the GRH Lean Handbook (github.com/tamnd/grh-lean-handbook at 152bdf2a), which cut this edition along the same folders.

children.title: The statements and the last step
children.summary: src/Statements.lean (imports only Mathlib: the four Prop definitions the theorems are stated with), src/Main.lean (the five theorems, each one line) and src/New/Main.lean (from no zero in re s > 1/2 to zeros on the line, by the functional equation). Their cone is the whole tree, since Main imports everything.
children.align: README: 'To trust the result, read src/Statements.lean ... the five statements in src/Main.lean'; Handbook vol. 0

children.title: Endgame: from a one-sided prime bound to the zeros
children.summary: The analytic end of the proof, and the only part that talks about zeros. A weighted sum over prime powers n = 1 mod q, with the non-negative weight Lambda(n)(1 - (n/d)), has a remainder R_q(x). Its Laplace transform has simple poles at the zeros of the L-functions mod q, with the zeros' orders as residues (up to a factor). Landau's lemma: a one-sided bound R_q(x) <= x^(beta - 1) and residues of one sign leave no zero in re s > beta. The twist by (./d) is chosen, by a zero-density count from Polya-Vinogradov, so that its zeros do not spoil the sign. Also here: the classical zero-free region and a Tauberian theorem (the prime number theorem with error, used at the second cut-off), and the symmetry of zeros from the functional equation.
children.align: GUIDE: 'From a one-sided bound to the zeros (Zeros)'; Handbook vol. 1 (in part) and vol. 2 'Analytic number theory' (Lib/Analytic)

children.title: The criterion and the prime-sum remainder
children.summary: New/Reduction/Zeros: the remainder R_q and its poles (PrimeError), the one-sided criterion LFunction_ne_zero_of_primeRemainder_le (Criterion), and the prime number theorem for the remainder at the second cut-off (PrimeNumberTheorem).

children.title: Analytic background on Dirichlet L-functions
children.summary: Lib/Analytic: Landau's lemma, the entire L-function and the residues of its log-derivative (the orders of its zeros), theta series and the functional equation in absolute value, Polya-Vinogradov, a zero-density count for quadratic twists in a box, primes in progressions, symmetry of zeros, and the prime number theorem (crude zero-free region, Tauberian step, growth near re s = 1). No Hadamard product, no zero-counting function N(T), no explicit formula over zeros.

children.title: The reduction: data, lattices and the main inequality
children.summary: New/Reduction outside Zeros. The admissible data (a CM field E, places, levels, twists and the scales x << x1 << b), heights and twisted lattices, the prime sums that are compared, and the main inequality star_inequality: one covolume, corrected by an index, bounded from above (Theorems A and B) and from below (Theorem C); the main amount cancels and the prime-sum remainder is bounded above. OneSidedBound turns it into R_q(x) <= x^(-1/2 + eps) and ends with grh. This is the one interface between the endgame and the automorphic machinery.
children.align: GUIDE: Reduction (Lattices, Data, PrimeSums, IntegralTargetForms, ShortAndEnough, MainInequality, OneSidedBound); Handbook vol. 1

children.title: Theorem A: short forms (the upper bound)
children.summary: A composite of m theta lifts between definite hermitian spaces, its divisibility (a seesaw identity, Stepanov's count of zeros in the root lemma) and its size: a multiple of the projected Poincare series has short lifts and a small index. Derivatives of theta functions count primes; this is where the prime sum enters the size.
children.align: GUIDE: 'Upper bound: a composite lift' and 'Derivatives of theta functions'; Handbook vol. 9 (New/UpperBound, New/Derivatives without Sharpness)

children.title: Upper bound: a composite lift
children.summary: New/UpperBound: theta kernels, source and target forms, chains of lifts, the seesaw identity, divisibility and size of the composite lift, elementary divisors of a Hecke operator.

children.title: Derivatives of theta functions
children.summary: New/Derivatives (without Sharpness): derivatives that count primes, the field and its characters, the formal group and the exponential factor, the integral vacuum.

children.title: Theorem B: enough forms (a second moment)
children.summary: New/Spanning: few translates of Poincare series span almost all target forms. A Petersson-type second moment, equality of multiplicities of Hecke eigensystems on two forms of one space, Bessel functions, unfolding, the main term and the remaining terms.
children.align: GUIDE: 'Spanning: a second moment'; Handbook vol. 10

children.title: Theorem C: long forms (the lower bound)
children.summary: Integral forms are long: the covolume and twice the index are at least about the main amount. A twist for each prime, norms of theta lifts, an exchange identity of Siegel-Weil type, the norm of a chain of lifts, one lift and its Hecke L-values, and congruences: Galois representations, Selmer groups of anticyclotomic twists, lifting crystalline classes.
children.align: GUIDE: 'Lower bound: the determinant', 'Lower bound: one lift', 'Lower bound: congruences'; Handbook vols. 11 and 12

children.title: The determinant
children.summary: New/Determinant: a twist for each prime, norms of theta lifts, the exchange identity, the norm of a chain, auxiliary forms; Theorem C itself (Twist/LongForms).

children.title: One lift
children.summary: New/OneLift: one lift and Hecke values, the comparison operator, periods of false lifts, Hecke L-values as squared norms and their valuations.

children.title: The bound is attained
children.summary: New/Derivatives/Sharpness: the divisibility bound of Theorem A is attained, as the lower bound needs.

children.title: Congruences and Selmer groups
children.summary: New/Congruences: the choice of twists, congruences and Galois representations, first-order congruences, anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups, the local loss, lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight. Its denominator bound uses odd classes only; the even classes, where Vandiver's conjecture lives, do not enter (FirstOrder/DenominatorBound, head).

children.title: Supplement: discrete series with a large gap
children.summary: New/Appendix: discrete series representations with a large gap between weights, used by Theorems B and C.
children.align: GUIDE: Appendix; Handbook vol. 5 (with the representations)

children.title: Background theories Mathlib lacks (src/Lib)
children.summary: Results classed as known in the literature, with their proofs, often in a weaker form that suffices here and with the development's own definitions. Lib imports nothing from New. Grouped as the Handbook's volumes 3 to 8 group them; Lib/Analytic is under the endgame.
children.align: GUIDE: section 1, last paragraph; Handbook vols. 3-8

children.title: Number fields, class field theory, CM
children.summary: Lib/ClassField, Lib/Cyclotomic, Lib/CM: class field theory and duality (artin_reciprocity), odd classes over cyclotomic fields, complex multiplication and a Chowla-Selberg formula.

children.title: Unitary groups and automorphic forms
children.summary: Lib/Adelic and Lib/General/Groups: adeles, unitary groups, automorphic forms, Hecke eigenforms, a simple trace formula.

children.title: Representations of real, p-adic and finite groups
children.summary: Lib/DiscreteSeries (without Theta), Lib/GLn, Lib/LocalGL: discrete series, Green's characters of GL_r over finite fields, local representations.

children.title: The theta correspondence and Siegel-Weil
children.summary: Lib/Weil, Lib/SiegelWeil, Lib/DiscreteSeries/Theta: the Weil representation, theta lifts, the Siegel-Weil and Rallis formulas.

children.title: Cohomology and p-adic Hodge theory
children.summary: Lib/Cohomology, Lib/PadicHodge, Lib/PadicComparison, Lib/General/Geometry, Lib/General/Algebra: l-adic and Hodge cohomology, p-adic comparison, Kisin modules.

children.title: Shimura varieties and Galois representations
children.summary: Lib/Shimura, Lib/GaloisRep: models of Shimura varieties and the Galois representations of eigenforms, matched to Hecke polynomials for most Frobenii only.

children.title: General mathematics and global settings
children.summary: The rest of Lib/General (analysis, linear algebra, measure, number theory, topology, combinatorics), Lib/Base and Lib/Speed (instance priorities and simp settings for the whole development; the authors report that everything still compiles with Speed emptied).
children.align: no Handbook volume of its own
